rationale: ONTOLOGY follow-up. Pins the `imports` edge's metadata when one MODULE is imported SCOPED more than once — the case where a single-valued `scopedItem` copied from the first statement is partial and reads as though it named them all. Source lines are load-bearing: import statements at 37 (`import struct Single.Alpha`), 38 (`import struct Single.Beta`), 39 (`import let Pair.Gamma`), 40 (`import let Pair.Delta`), 41 (`import Solo`), 42 (`import struct Single.Epsilon`). The grammar shapes are probe-verified by script/m14/swift-grammar-shape-probe.ts; the population the rule answers is measured over the three swift corpora — 25 (file, module) pairs scope-import one module 2+ times, the largest being swift-nio's Sources/NIOCore/BSDSocketAPI.swift with 37 scoped WinSDK imports. PINS-FORBIDS authored from re-probed emission per M34 requirement 4: the forbids are the shapes a per-statement rule or a module rule with a partial field would produce.

expectRelationships.comment: THE row this fixture exists for: three scoped imports of one module are ONE edge, so `scopedItem` is absent — publishing `Alpha` would name one of three and read as all of them. `scopedItemCount` states the size of what the edge does not enumerate. `scopedKind` and `moduleSpecifier` still describe the first statement and are true of it.
the rule is about ANY module scoped 2+ times, not a particular count; the `let` scope kind proves the token read is the grammar's and not a substring of the path
an UNSCOPED import grows no count field and no scope kind — a rule that stamped `scopedItemCount` on every module would fail this row
`references` is PER STATEMENT and names the SPELLED path; 6 statements produce 6 edges while only 3 modules are involved
the third scoped import of `Single` adds a `references` edge and no second `imports` edge — the two labels are visibly different rules over one file

forbidRelationships.comment: the MODULE is the edge target; the spelled path lives in metadata.moduleSpecifier. A dotted target is the R10 failure go documents (`net/http`).
THE pin for the rule: no `imports` edge may carry a single-valued `scopedItem` while its module is scoped more than once. Dropping `scopedItem` is the honest answer; publishing one of N is not.
no count field on an unscoped module — `equals`-style pins cannot say 'absent', so the absent case is pinned here

expectRelationshipCount.comment: three statements, one MODULE, one edge
two statements, one module, one edge
exactly 3 module edges in the file: Single, Pair, Solo. A per-statement rule would publish 6.
`references` stays per statement: 6 import statements yield 6 references edges naming 6 spelled paths
the pair of totals (3 imports vs 6 references) is what says the two labels are not the same fact under two names
